children: Euro zone bond yields were broadly steady on Wednesday while their US counterparts eased as Democrats gained control of both the Senate and the House in the US midterm elections, with European investors also awaiting fresh regional inflation data.

The outcome of the midterm elections could hold broad implications for market-sensitive areas including the AI data-center buildout, the US fiscal outlook, defense spending and regulation in areas such as healthcare, banking and cryptocurrencies.
Markets also weighed the potential for legislative gridlock between US President Donald Trump's administration and the newly elected Democratic Congress.

Elsewhere, Brent crude futures were little changed on the day at $104.35 a barrel after falling for two consecutive sessions, as investors awaited Washington's next move in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
German 10-year government bond yields (DE10YT=RR) were last little changed at 3.3108%.

Euro zone inflation data is due later in the session, and is expected to show a rise in October from September's 3.8%. Economists polled by Reuters are expecting October's flash reading to come in at 4%.

The European Central Bank opted to keep rates steady last week, but another hike could come in December with a growing list of policymakers backing such a move. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said on Tuesday evening that "from today's perspective, an interest rate hike in December is very likely necessary."
"There seems to be little alternative to an interest rate hike unless the inflation outlook improves significantly," he said.
Money markets were last pricing in a roughly 70% probability of a December hike.
Germany's 2-year government bond yield (DE2YT=RR), which is typically more sensitive to interest rate expectations, was steady at 3.0167%.
